body:
A burnt taste is unpleasant, and it is a clear sign that something is off in your setup. It happens when the cotton wick or the liquid on the coil gets too hot, and it is almost always preventable. This guide explains what is actually happening inside the device when a vape tastes burnt, the common causes in the order you should check them, how to fix each one, how to avoid damaging a new coil, why chain vaping and thick liquid cause problems, how to tell a burnt coil from a dying battery, what not to do and how to prevent the problem. It is written for adults aged 21 and over. Nicotine is addictive, and nothing here is medical advice.

## What a burnt taste actually is
When the coil heats, liquid in the wick absorbs the heat and turns to vapor. If there is not enough liquid in the wick, the cotton itself heats, and it scorches, giving a harsh, acrid, sometimes bitter taste. Sugars and sweeteners in the liquid can also caramelize on the coil when they sit on it too long or too hot, leaving a residue that tastes burnt on later puffs. In both cases, the taste is a signal that the coil is not being cooled by liquid as it should be.

## Dry or low liquid
If liquid runs low, the wick dries and burns. Refill or replace before the pod or tank empties, and keep the level above the minimum line. In a device with a window, check it before you use it. In a disposable, a burnt taste late in its life may mean the liquid is nearly finished, and it is time to replace the device.

## An unprimed coil
A new coil needs time to soak. Without priming, the dry cotton scorches on the first puffs, which can ruin a coil in seconds. See [how to prime a coil](/blog/how-to-prime-a-new-coil-or-pod/). Drip a few drops on the cotton, fill the tank or pod and wait, then start with gentle puffs at a low power.

## Chain vaping
Rapid puffs without letting the wick re-saturate can burn it. The wick can only draw liquid in as fast as it can move, and long, repeated puffs use it faster. Take breaks between puffs, and use shorter draws. If you tend to chain vape, a device with better wicking, or a larger coil, may suit you better.

## Wrong liquid for the coil
Thick, sugary or high-VG liquid can struggle to wick through small coils, and sweeteners caramelize on the heating surface. Match liquid to hardware: high-VG liquids suit sub-ohm tanks with large wicking openings, and 50/50 or PG-leaning liquids suit pods. See [PG and VG ratios](/blog/pg-vg-ratio-explained/). Very sweet dessert liquids are tougher on coils, and they shorten coil life even when used correctly.

## Too much power
Running above the coil's recommended wattage burns cotton fast. If your device lets you set power, lower it to the middle of the coil's range or below. If it is a fixed-power pod, the maker has set it, and a burnt taste points to another cause. See [ohms, watts and volts](/blog/what-are-ohms-watts-and-volts-in-vaping/).

## A worn coil
Coils that have been in use a while build up residue. Even with good liquid levels, a coil with a caked surface gives a burnt taste. Replace it. See [how often to replace coils](/blog/how-often-to-replace-coils/). A coil that tastes burnt from new, though, may be unprimed or faulty.

## Blocked or tight airflow
Too little airflow can cause the coil to overheat, because there is not enough air to carry heat away. Open the airflow slightly, or check that nothing blocks it. See [adjustable airflow explained](/blog/adjustable-airflow-explained/).

## Low battery
As a battery weakens, some devices deliver uneven power, which can cause odd tastes. If the burnt taste appears together with weak vapor at low charge, charge the device and test again.

## How to tell whether the coil is the problem
Try a fresh coil or pod. If the burnt taste goes away, the old coil was the problem. If it stays, check the liquid level, the liquid type and the power. Changing one thing at a time tells you which it is. If you have two devices, try the same liquid in the other, to see if the liquid is the cause.

## A step-by-step fix
1. Stop vaping, because more puffs will make it worse.
2. Check the liquid level and top up if needed.
3. Let the coil rest for a few minutes to re-saturate.
4. Take a gentle puff to test.
5. If it is still burnt, lower the power or open the airflow.
6. If it is still burnt, replace the coil or pod.
7. Prime the new coil properly.

## What not to do
Do not keep vaping through a burnt taste. It will not improve, it can be unpleasant to inhale and it wears out the coil faster. Do not add more power to try to burn off the taste, which makes it worse. Do not rinse a coil with water and reuse it, because water and electrical parts do not mix, and a wet coil can misfire. Do not try to clean a coil with flames or heat.

## Prevention
Prime coils, keep pods filled and use compatible liquid. Take steady puffs with breaks. Keep power in range. Replace coils on a schedule that suits your use. Store devices upright. Keep a spare pod or coil so that a burnt one can be replaced right away. Browse [coils and pods](/shop/coils-pods/) for replacements.

## Frequently asked questions in depth
### Why does a new coil taste burnt?
Usually it was not primed, or it was used at too high a power before it was soaked. Let it rest and use low power.

### Can a burnt coil recover?
Sometimes a mild case recovers after resting and re-saturating. A truly burnt coil does not, and it should be replaced.

### Why does my disposable taste burnt at the end?
The liquid is probably nearly finished. A burnt taste is a sign that the wick is running dry.

### Do some flavors burn more easily?
Sweet, creamy and dessert flavors leave more residue and can taste burnt sooner. That is a property of the recipe, not a fault.

### Is a burnt taste harmful?
We make no health claims. A burnt taste is unpleasant and a sign that the device is not working as intended, so stop and fix the cause.

## Related
See [why a vape is not hitting](/blog/why-is-my-vape-not-hitting/), [dry hits explained](/blog/dry-hits-explained/) and [vape flavor fading fixes](/blog/vape-flavor-fading-fixes/). All products are for adults aged 21 and over, and nicotine is addictive.

## Case studies
### The new coil that tasted burnt
A customer fitted a new coil and fired it straight away. The first puffs tasted burnt, and they carried on. By the end of the day the coil was ruined. Priming for ten minutes and starting at a low power would have prevented it. Lesson: the first minutes of a coil's life decide how long it lasts.

### The sweet liquid that kept burning coils
A customer using a very sweet dessert liquid found that coils lasted only three days. Switching to a less sweet liquid doubled coil life, and lowering the power by a few watts helped too. Lesson: some liquids are hard on coils, and the fix may be the liquid, not the coil.

### The disposable that tasted burnt at the end
A large disposable tasted burnt after several weeks. The liquid window showed it nearly empty. The device had simply reached the end of its liquid. Lesson: a burnt taste late in a device's life often means it is finished.

## A weekly habit check
Check liquid levels before you start vaping each day, give a new coil a proper soak, replace a coil when the taste changes and keep a spare. These four habits prevent most burnt tastes.

## When flavor is the problem, not burning
Not every unpleasant taste is burnt. A flat or muddy taste can mean a worn coil or a flavor you have tired of. A soapy or chemical taste can come from residue after cleaning. A sour taste can come from old liquid. Learn to tell them apart: burnt is sharp and acrid, flat is dull, soapy is smooth and unpleasant, and sour is tangy. See [vape flavor fading fixes](/blog/vape-flavor-fading-fixes/).

## Frequently asked questions about taste
### Can e-liquid itself taste burnt?
Old or overheated liquid can taste off, and a liquid that has darkened a lot may taste harsher. If the same liquid tastes fine in another device, the liquid is not the cause.

### Why does a burnt taste come and go?
It can appear when the wick is drying between puffs, and disappear after a rest. That pattern points to wicking, liquid thickness or chain vaping.

### Should I change liquid flavors to fix it?
A very sweet or very thick flavor may be the cause. Try a thinner or less sweet liquid before you replace the coil again.

### Is it worth switching to a bigger coil?
If you chain vape or use thick liquids, a coil with better wicking can help. Match it to your device and liquid.

faq.q: Why does my vape taste burnt?
faq.a: Usually a dry wick, an unprimed or worn coil, chain vaping, too much power or liquid that is too thick for the coil.
Check the liquid level, let the coil rest, lower the power or open the airflow, and replace the coil if it persists.

faq.q: Can I keep using a burnt coil?
faq.a: No. It will not improve and wears out faster. Replace it.
Prime new coils, keep liquid above the minimum, avoid chain vaping and use liquid that suits the coil.

faq.q: Why do sweet liquids burn coils faster?
faq.a: Sweeteners caramelize on the heating surface and leave residue that tastes burnt.

faq.q: Should I clean the coil with water?
faq.a: No. Water and electrical parts do not mix. Replace the coil.
